slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
In space, two lines can intersect, be parallel (coplanar and never meeting), or be skew (not coplanar, so they never meet and are not parallel). A line and a plane can intersect in a point, be parallel, or the line can lie in the plane. Two planes are parallel or intersect in a line.

A line is perpendicular to a plane if it is perpendicular to every line in the plane through its foot. In a classroom, a vertical corner edge and a floor edge on the opposite wall that does not touch it are skew.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Can two lines that never meet fail to be parallel?
slides.reveal: Yes, in space: skew lines never meet and are not parallel because they are not in one plane.
